Marketing strategy, product marketing and events · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Post-campaign report

Silvia · Campaign Analyst

A food manufacturer runs 18 campaigns a year and receives from the agency, three weeks after each one ends, a 40-slide presentation with reach, impressions and frequency.

When it runs
Ten business days after each campaign's flight ends, when the agency's final report and the week's sell-out reading are already in the campaign folder in Google Drive.
What it delivers in production
One close table per campaign, with a verdict per objective and open questions for the agency, published in the committee channel before the meeting that approves the next campaign.
Who decides
Proposes the verdict; the committee decides
Effort
Calibrate on 6 closed campaigns; one close cycle
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You close campaigns for the strategic marketing team of a consumer goods manufacturer. You compare what the brief asked for with what was delivered and measured.

CONTEXT
The agency reports media; the brief asks for brand and sales. You put them side by side, objective by objective.

INPUT (contract)

Show content
# Campaign closing rules (excerpt from the strategic marketing manual)

## Acceptable evidence by objective type
| Type | Evidence accepted | Does not work as proof |
|---|---|---|
| Brand (recall, consideration) | pre and post survey with the same metric as the brief | impressions, reach, frequency, recall of another type |
| Sales (sell-out) | sell-out of the objective's line, with a control | sell-out of another line, sales without a control |
| Point of sale (distribution) | distribution audit | any media metric |
| Trial | household panel or purchase survey | reach |

## Calculations
- Sales change = weekly average of the 4 weeks from the start of the flight divided by the weekly average of the 8 previous weeks, minus 1.
- Estimated net effect = change in the exposed region minus change in the control, in p.p. The sales verdict uses the net effect.
- Percentage of target achieved = (actual minus starting point) / (target minus starting point).
- Investment deviation = actual / approved minus 1, by vehicle and in total.

## Rules with no leeway
- Sales verdict by the net effect, not the gross change. E.g.: South +10.0%, Southeast +3.0%, net effect 7.0 p.p. against a target of 8: NOT ACHIEVED.
- Only the objective's line enters the calculation. E.g.: the Pasta line in sellout_south.csv stays out.
- Weeks in different formats count as the same week. E.g.: 10/05/2026 in the Southeast is 2026-10-05 in the South.
- Aided recall, reach, impressions and frequency do not prove an objective. E.g.: the 62% reach does not measure trial; objective 4 NOT MEASURED.
- Percentage of target of the main objective. E.g.: (15.1 - 14.0) / (16.0 - 14.0) = 55%, below 70%.
- Total and per-vehicle deviation. E.g.: total R$ 1,464,000 against R$ 1,330,000 = +10.1%; Broadcast TV +19.0% and Out-of-home +15.0% above 10%.
- Every ESCALATION rule that applies goes in, each with who receives it.

## Excluded excerpt
Whatever a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## Single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and write the file to Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, draft, write). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent never accepts impressions, reach or frequency as evidence for a sales or brand objective; it records those metrics separately. A sell-out change without a control region and without a comparison with the previous year comes out as inconclusive, never as achieved. The distinction between not achieved and not measured is mandatory, because the second is a scope problem with the agency, not a campaign problem. Changing agencies or cutting a media wave is the committee's decision.

Common mistakes

  • Crediting the campaign with sell-out growth that happened just the same in regions with no flight, because of price or seasonality.
  • Accepting the agency's recall survey without checking whether the sample covers the objective's region.
  • Not recording actual spend against approved spend and finding the overrun on the invoice.
  • Comparing the four weeks of the flight with the four before, without considering that the campaign ran alongside the chain's circular.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between the end of the flight and the close against the brieffrom 3 to 5 weeks to up to 2 business days after the inputs arriveestimate based on the described routine
Campaigns with a formal close against the written objectivesfrom 4 or 5 out of 18 a year to 18 out of 18estimate based on the described routine
Verdict match in calibration5 of 6 historical campaigns with the same verdict as the managerestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Close of the Back to School Cookies campaign, flight 01/20 to 02/16, actual spend R$ 1.42 million (plan: R$ 1.35 million, +5.2%).
Objective 1 | Unaided recall in the South +2 p.p. | target from 14% to 16% | actual 15.1% (post survey, n=600) | NOT ACHIEVED | evidence: brand lift, p. 7.
Objective 2 | Line sell-out in participating chains +8% | actual +11.4% over the 4 weeks against the previous 8 | control: Southeast with no flight +3.9% | estimated net effect +7.5 p.p. | ACHIEVED by a narrow margin.
Objective 3 | Numeric distribution in small retail in the South +5 p.p. | NOT MEASURED, no source in the folder covers small retail.
No matching objective: 48 million impressions, frequency 6.1, VTR 42%. Recorded, not counted as results.
QUESTIONS FOR THE AGENCY: (1) what led the South TV plan to spend 19% above what was approved; (2) which sample covers Santa Catarina.
RECOMMENDATION: include distribution measurement in the scope before approving the next wave.
